name: The Lord of the Rings
hook: One Ring, three volumes, and the Oxford philologist who invented Middle-earth.

facts.label: J.R.R. Tolkien
facts.statement: Tolkien was an Oxford philologist who invented languages and taught at Leeds and Oxford; Bag End takes its name from his Aunt Jane's farm.

facts.label: the One Ring
facts.statement: The title's dark lord is Sauron; in The Hobbit the ring was merely a magic ring of invisibility, but in the trilogy it is the One Ring.

facts.label: The Fellowship of the Ring
facts.statement: The first volume (1954) says its prologue is 'largely concerned with hobbits'; the Fellowship's elven archer is Legolas, son of Thranduil.

facts.label: The Two Towers
facts.statement: The middle volume builds to the battle of Helm's Deep and Treebeard's Ents attacking Saruman's forces.

facts.label: The Return of the King
facts.statement: The 1955 finale ends with Frodo and Sam approaching Mount Doom; Peter Jackson's 2003 film won 11 Oscars.

facts.label: Gandalf
facts.statement: Gandalf is the wizard who sacrifices himself by breaking the bridge he stands on, falling into the abyss with the Balrog.

facts.label: The Silmarillion
facts.statement: Published posthumously in 1977, The Silmarillion is a prequel telling Middle-earth's First Age.
